title: Count Primes Below n
summary: How many primes are smaller than n?
statement: Return the number of prime numbers strictly less than `n`.
hints: Testing each number separately is slow for large n. Can you rule out many numbers at once?
The Sieve of Eratosthenes: for each prime p, cross out p*p, p*p+p, ... as composite.

composite = [false] * n
count = 0
for i in 2..n-1:
    if not composite[i]:
        count += 1
        for j in range(i*i, n, i): composite[j] = true
return count
The sieve runs in O(n log log n) with O(n) memory. Starting at `i * i` is enough because smaller multiples were crossed out by smaller primes. Use a long for `i * i`.
